\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یادداشت} \fa{کردن} (yâddâsht kardan)}{یادداشت کردن (yâddâsht kardan)}]{\fa{یادداشت} \fa{کردن} (yâddâsht kardan) — to note down}

\label{lesson:FA-C188-yaddasht-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to save, then the Persian for to deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یادداشت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{یادداشت} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{yâddâsht kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to note down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yâddâsht kardan} pairs \emph{yâddâsht}, \textquotedblleft{}note\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan}. \emph{yâddâsht} is \emph{yâd}, \textquotedblleft{}memory\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{dâsht}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{dâshtan}): a memory-keeper. All are native Persian. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to save, then the Persian for to deposit, then say \emph{yâddâsht kardan} again
